candidates.name: keepa (Python client)
candidates.what_it_holds: Python client library (Apache-2.0, 227 commits, active) wrapping the Keepa API to pull per-ASIN Amazon price history, sales-rank (BSR) history, offer/buy-box history, and current listing details; includes async support and matplotlib plotting of history series. No data committed — it is a method to acquire time-series price/rank history, but requires a PAID Keepa subscription and API key to actually pull data.
candidates.why_useful: Amazon sales-rank history is the closest real-world analogue to nowcasting a platform's unit volume from a public/paid third-party index (like AirDNA for STRs, gap #2). Even though it needs a paid key, the repo is a template for how such point-in-time rank/price panels are structured and queried, and the wrapper pattern (ASIN -> time series of rank+price) is directly reusable if the team ever gets a comparable STR-panel API.
candidates.time_coverage: however far back a Keepa subscription's history buffer extends (years, per Keepa's own limits)
candidates.geography: Amazon marketplaces (US and others depending on subscription)
candidates.last_activity: active (227 commits, workflow/CI present; exact date not surfaced)

candidates.name: tranco-list (Tranco ranking generator)
candidates.what_it_holds: Source code (Python: combined_lists.py, generate_daily_list.py, job_handler.py/job_server.py, generate_domain_parts.py) that produces the daily Tranco top-1M website ranking, a research-oriented, manipulation-hardened alternative to Alexa/Similarweb rankings; the live ranking lists themselves are served from tranco-list.eu (daily-updated, historical lists downloadable by date from that companion site), with the generation code open on GitHub.
candidates.why_useful: Directly matches CONTEXT gap #5 ("Tranco / Common Crawl host-graph ranks") as an engagement/traffic-rank proxy; a historical Tranco pull for airbnb.com vs. booking.com/expedia.com/vrbo.com domains could serve as a crude relative web-traffic-momentum indicator ahead of prints, and this repo is the citable source/generation method plus pointer to the historical list archive.
candidates.license: not shown on the fetched page (check repo LICENSE file before quoting)
candidates.last_activity: low commit count (4 on master) but the hosted list itself updates daily
candidates.size_hint: code repo small; each daily list ~1M domain-rank rows, hosted externally

candidates.name: Tranco top-sites list (hosted archive)
candidates.what_it_holds: Companion site to the GitHub repo above; lets you generate/download a historical Tranco top-1M ranking list for any past date, and links a community Go client (WangYihang/tranco-go-package) plus the Python client (tranco-list/tranco-python, page 404'd on direct check).
candidates.why_useful: Same as the tranco-list repo above — external host for the actual point-in-time ranking snapshots by date, which is what would be needed for a genuine time series (gap #4/#5, vintage engagement data).
candidates.time_coverage: historical daily snapshots, generatable on demand
candidates.license: academic/research use per Tranco paper (Le Pochat et al.)

candidates.name: CrUX (Chrome UX Report community repo)
candidates.what_it_holds: Community hub (Apache-2.0, 219 stars, 47 forks) of SQL queries for BigQuery, JS API-call snippets, AppScript, and Jupyter Colabs for pulling Chrome UX Report data — real-user web performance AND site-popularity histograms (CrUX includes a per-origin popularity rank/tier) published monthly by Google. No raw data committed (BigQuery/API pull), but ready-made queries.
candidates.why_useful: Matches gap #5 ("Chrome UX Report popularity rank") exactly; CrUX's origin popularity ranking (rank buckets by real Chrome traffic) is a free, monthly, historically-versioned alternative/complement to Similarweb-style traffic estimates for airbnb.com and competitor domains.
candidates.time_coverage: CrUX dataset itself goes back to ~Oct 2017, monthly, on BigQuery (public dataset, this repo is tooling only)
candidates.license: Apache-2.0 (repo); CrUX data itself is Google's public BigQuery dataset (ODC-BY-like terms)
candidates.last_activity: active, 219 stars / 47 forks, open issues present
candidates.size_hint: tooling only in this repo; underlying BigQuery tables are large (public dataset)

candidates.name: python-mwviews (Wikipedia pageviews client)
candidates.what_it_holds: MIT-licensed Python client (PageviewsClient, 38 commits) for the Wikimedia Foundation pageview API: pulls article_views, project_views, top_articles, top_by_country, and top_per_country at daily or monthly granularity for arbitrary date ranges, with ThreadPoolExecutor parallelization for bulk pulls.
candidates.why_useful: Matches gap #5 ("Wikipedia pageviews tooling"); pageviews on the "Airbnb", "Vrbo", "Booking.com" etc. Wikipedia articles, or on destination-city pages, are a free, long-history, point-in-time-stable (dumps are dated) engagement/interest proxy that complements (and is less noisy for point-in-time purposes than) Google Trends, which the team already found not to work as pulled.
candidates.time_coverage: Wikimedia pageview API goes back to July 2015 (hourly/daily dumps)
candidates.last_activity: not shown precisely; repo is small/mature (38 commits)
candidates.size_hint: code only; API returns arbitrary-size JSON per query

candidates.name: Olist Brazilian E-Commerce public dataset (source repo)
candidates.what_it_holds: MIT-licensed repo (the original source behind the well-known Kaggle "Brazilian E-Commerce Public Dataset by Olist") holding sample relational tables extracted from Olist's real marketplace: orders, order items/prices, freight value, products, sellers (9,000+), customers, and reviews, covering hundreds of thousands of orders across Brazil; includes an ER-diagram schema.
candidates.why_useful: A real (not synthetic) multi-table ecommerce marketplace transaction dataset with prices, freight/shipping cost, seller counts, delivery times and customer reviews by Brazilian region — useful as a structural template for how a two-sided marketplace's take-rate/logistics-cost/review data can be organized, and as a LatAm regional ecommerce-activity dataset in its own right (LatAm demand is gap #7).
candidates.time_coverage: 2016-2018 order history (per the well-known Kaggle companion release; exact span not restated on this page)
candidates.license: MIT (repo); Kaggle release under CC BY-NC-SA
candidates.last_activity: not shown; used as a stable hiring-assessment reference dataset
candidates.size_hint: hundreds of thousands of orders, 950,000+ products, 9,000+ sellers per repo description

candidates.name: Ecommerce-Price-Tracker
candidates.what_it_holds: Small modular Python pipeline (no stars, updated Jul 2026) that scrapes real-time prices across e-commerce sites, cleans them into structured CSV-like outputs, computes historical trend charts. No data files committed as of the check; purely a scraping/ETL template.
candidates.why_useful: Low-value on its own (no data, generic personal project) but is a concrete, current (2026) template for a lightweight scheduled price-scrape-to-timeseries pipeline, structurally similar to what would be needed for any non-Airbnb STR-price-panel scraper the team might build later.

notes: This scout hit two hard blockers: (1) the shared WebSearch budget was already exhausted (200/200) before any of my WebSearch calls ran, so all queries fell back to other tools per the task's fallback ladder; (2) the DuckDuckGo html.duckduckgo.com endpoint gave connect ECONNREFUSED on both attempts (network/routing issue, not a query problem), Bing's site: filter did not survive the WebFetch markdown-summarization step (the summarizer returned generic 'no relevant results' descriptions rather than the actual filtered SERPs), and github.com/search itself started 429-rate-limiting after two calls. I used all 4 permitted `gh search repos` calls; those surfaced almost exclusively low-quality one-off student EDA/Power-BI notebooks on generic 'Amazon product dataset' Kaggle mirrors (no unique data, no time series, no rank/price history) — consistent with the exclusion criteria, so I did not list most of them. Given search-tool degradation, I pivoted to direct WebFetch verification of specific repos recalled from general knowledge (Keepa, Tranco, CrUX, python-mwviews, Olist) plus one gh-search hit (Ecommerce-Price-Tracker); all verified as real, existing, non-dead repos. I was NOT able to verify some other repos I considered (McAuley-Lab/Amazon-Reviews-2023 404'd at the guessed path — the real Amazon Reviews 2023 dataset almost certainly exists at a slightly different org/path and is worth a follow-up scout with working search; tranco-list/tranco-python also 404'd, likely renamed/moved). A follow-up scout on this theme, once the WebSearch budget resets, should specifically chase: (a) the correct URL for the McAuley-Lab Amazon Reviews 2023 dataset (very large, real product metadata incl. price/category, would be high-value as an ecommerce-KPI-panel template), (b) SimilarWeb-style third-party scraper repos (the official similarweb GitHub org has no such repos — only internal devops tooling), (c) Datafiniti/Webhose sample ecommerce product-price exports, (d) any GitHub mirror of the discontinued Amazon 'movers and shakers' or bestsellers historical snapshots. None of the candidates found directly touch Airbnb; all are offered as engagement/rank/price-panel *templates* per the theme brief.
